Landmark of a 4th Class, poor Town of Gabaldon:Valley Breeze Resort[1] is a landmark, interesting point of Gabaldon; a 3.3 hectare family resort in a valley[2][3][

at the foot of the Sierra Madre mountains. Located 171 kilometers from Metro Manila or Baguio, Valley Breeze Resort provides nipa hut designed cottage accommodations; an experience of farm life; educational tour of a rice field, vegetable farm, and typical farm animals; collection of birds around a manmade lake and boating. Fish feeding and fishing; Swimming pools for children and adults with restaurant and huts; 20 ft slide; the pool water is sourced from the sparkling and clear mineral springs of Nueva Ecija; Karaoke Kiosk.

- at Barangay Malinao, Gabaldon, Nueva Ecija[4] (formerly Sabani and Bitulok) is a fourth class municipality in the province of Nueva Ecija, Philippines; it has a population of 32,246 people in 2010. Ilog Carugang (Carugang River) serves as the gateway to Sitio Carugang, a far-off place in Gabaldon, Nueva Ecija. The river has been a silent witness to the harvesting of what the people of Carugang had sown, for merchants have to cross the river so they can buy the crops the farmers planted and reaped.[5]

pages.title: File:Villager Returning With Collected Saag From Rice Field - Preparation Of Traditional Santal Food Mela - 11th Museum Day Celebration - Museum Of Santal Culture - Birbhum 2024-12-08 01339.jpg

ObjectName.value: Villager Returning With Collected Saag From Rice Field - Preparation Of Traditional Santal Food Mela - 11th Museum Day Celebration - Museum Of Santal Culture - Birbhum 2024-12-08 01339

ImageDescription.value: Santiniketan, Birbhum, India– December 8, 2024: Santal Villagers Celebrate Heritage with Traditional Food Mela. Enthusiastic villagers from Bishnubati and Ghosaldanga gathered to prepare for the Traditional Santal Food Mela by collecting fresh saag from local paddy fields. The one-day food mela, featuring dishes prepared using traditional methods, was a highlight of the 11th Museum Day celebration at the Museum of Santal Culture in Bishnubati.The event, organized by the Ghosaldanga Bishnubati Adivasi Trust in collaboration with the Centre for Internet and Society, brought together community members in a joyful atmosphere. The celebration not only showcased Santal culinary traditions but also emphasized the importance of preserving and promoting the community’s rich heritage for future generations.The opening day witnessed vibrant festivities, uniting villagers and visitors alike in honoring the unique cultural identity of the Santal people.
